title: Jesus was not crucified alone.
paragraphs: Jesus was not crucified alone.
That detail matters more than most people realize.

He was placed between two criminals—
not by coincidence…
but by divine design.

Because the cross was never just about suffering.
It was about revelation.

Revelation of who Jesus is…
and revelation of who we are.

Three crosses stood on that hill.
But the real story wasn’t the wood, the nails, or even the pain.
It was the response.

On one side was a man who was broken…
but still proud.

He was dying, yet still defiant.
Close to Jesus—but unwilling to believe.

He looked at the same Savior,
heard the same words,
felt the same moment…
…and chose to mock Him.
“Are You not the Christ? Save Yourself and us.”
Notice this:
Pain does not automatically produce surrender.

Some people suffer…
and still harden their hearts.
Then there was the other criminal.

Just as guilty.
Just as broken.
Just as deserving of judgment.
But something shifted inside him.
In his final moments, clarity came.

He rebuked the other criminal and said:
“We are punished justly… for we are getting what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.” (Luke 23:41)
In other words:

One man defended his sin.
The other confessed it.
And then… he turned his head toward Jesus.

Not with pride.
Not with demands.
But with surrender.
“Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom.”
That sentence is powerful.
Because it reveals something most people miss:
He believed in a kingdom… while looking at a dying King.

There was no crown.
No throne.
No army.
No victory in sight.

Just blood.
Just nails.
Just a broken body hanging on wood.
And yet… he believed.
That is faith.

Not believing when things look powerful—
but believing when everything looks lost.
And Jesus responded with one of the most hope-filled promises in Scripture:
“Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in paradise.” (Luke 23:43)
Let that sink in.

A man who had lived a life of sin…
a man with no time to fix his past…
no time to prove himself…
no time to earn anything…
…was given eternal life in a moment.
Why?

Because salvation was never about performance.
It was always about surrender.

You don’t need time to be saved.
You need a heart that turns.
Now here’s where it gets personal.

Both criminals were equally close to Jesus.
The same distance.
The same exposure.
The same opportunity.
But only one was transformed.
Which means:
Being near Jesus is not the same as knowing Him.

You can grow up in church…
hear sermons…
know Scripture…
be surrounded by truth…
…and still reject Him.
Proximity does not equal relationship.
That’s a warning.
But it’s also an invitation.

Because no matter how far you think you’ve gone…
no matter how many mistakes you’ve made…
no matter how late you think it is…
it is not too late to turn.

That criminal had minutes left.
And it was enough.

Not because of who he was—
but because of who Jesus is.
And here’s the deeper picture:
Jesus was in the middle.

Not randomly placed—
but prophetically positioned.

Isaiah 53:12 says,
“He was numbered with the transgressors.”

He didn’t just die for sinners.
He died among them.
He stood in the middle because that’s where He stands for all of humanity:

Between guilt and grace.
Between judgment and mercy.
Between rebellion and repentance.

One man rejected Him.
One man received Him.
And that same choice still exists today.
Every day, people stand at the same crossroads.

Not on a hill called Golgotha—
but in the quiet decisions of their hearts.

Some mock.
Some ignore.
Some delay.
And some surrender.
The cross forces a response.
You cannot stay neutral forever.
Because eventually, every heart answers the same question:
What will you do with Jesus?
And here’s the truth that makes this message so powerful:

The difference between the two criminals
was not their past.
It was their posture.

One hardened.
One humbled.

One demanded.
One surrendered.

One died in sin.
One died in faith.

Same cross.
Different eternity.
Take a moment.

Not to admire the story—
but to locate yourself in it.

Are you resisting…
or are you surrendering?
Because Jesus is still in the middle.

Still offering grace.
Still extending mercy.
Still saving those who turn to Him—even now.
And just like that day on the cross…
your response will determine everything.

Engagement Question:
If you had to be honest—do you relate more to the first criminal or the second right now… and why?
